clue.text: Those hurtful things taken on board, bully can't set on kids

indicators.note: a thing taken on board ship goes inside it, so the shuffled letters are put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: being on board means being aboard ship, and SS is the abbreviation for a steamship

indicators.note: to bully is to push someone around, so the letters of the following words are pushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bully loads up a ship's cargo of nasty things, but cannot set them on the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully' reorders the letters of CAN'T SET ON KIDS into TICKSANDSTONE; 'taken on board' puts that within the steamship letters. The answer is the start of the playground rhyme about name-calling.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground rhyme says these may break your bones, unlike mere words, so they are the hurtful things it names.

clue.text: Broadcast covering party wearing a rigid American outfit?

indicators.note: the broadcast word wraps round everything that follows it

parts.note: to beam a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: the party word is worn inside the letters of 'a' plus the rigid word, like a garment around a body

parts.note: something set is fixed or rigid
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A broadcast shows a party where someone wears a stiff American costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' gives ASEBALLT; 'covering' then wraps the broadcast word round it. 'outfit' suggests clothing, but here it means a group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a group or organisation, and a sports team playing America's national game is one such group.

clue.text: See 2
A leg bandaged by lean skier, perhaps

indicators.note: the leg word is wrapped up inside the lean word, as a bandage wraps a limb

parts.note: to list is to lean over to one side, as a ship does
pins is slang for legs, so one leg is a pin

explanation.surface: A thin skier has an injured leg strapped up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer or skier in the high Alps; 'perhaps' marks a skier as one example of the kind.

clue.text: Roman emperor set empire's rule in bronze

indicators.note: to set a gem is to fix it within a mount, here the rule word fixed inside the colour word
the rule word sits in the bronze word

parts.note: tan is a bronze, sun-darkened colour
the Raj was British rule over the Indian empire

explanation.surface: An emperor has his empire's law cast in bronze.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan ruled the Roman Empire from AD 98 to 117 and is remembered for his column in Rome.

clue.text: Awfully cross, in a stupor

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly angry while dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a drug-induced state of unconsciousness or drowsiness, which is a stupor.

clue.text: One rule I had lifted for religious festival

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the words raises them so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a law is a rule
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: One rule I had has been relaxed for a religious holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, held each autumn.

clue.text: 20 18, card of countless torments

indicators.note: to torment something is to twist and rack it, so the preceding words' letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A playing card that brings endless suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 20 and 18 together give NINE OF DIAMONDS, the card with this traditional nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine of diamonds has long been nicknamed with this phrase, for reasons historians still dispute.

clue.text: Tourist, one tangling with traffic initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word traffic

parts.note: to ravel is to tangle, so one who tangles is a raveller

explanation.surface: A tourist tangles with the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone journeying away from home, a synonym in the broad sense.

clue.text: I'm leaving, stop breaking my heart?

indicators.note: the stop word breaks into the middle of the heart letters
the heart of a word is its middle, so the setter's name loses its outer letters

parts.note: the setter is Paul, so 'my' from his viewpoint stands for his own name
to die is to stop, as an engine does

explanation.surface: A departing lover begs not to have their heart broken.
explanation.walkthrough: AU, the heart of PAUL, is broken by DIE. Setters often use 'my' or 'me' for their own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, said by someone announcing their departure.

clue.text: At home, unknown character occupying new home in Jersey etc

indicators.note: everything before sits in the island letters

parts.note: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI

indicators.note: the unknown letter occupies a place inside the shuffled home letters
new indicates the letters of home are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so z is one unknown character

explanation.surface: An unknown person moves into a new house in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the four letters into HEMO before the unknown letter is placed in it. The definition's 'home' is reused by the setter as fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means at my house, a direct translation.

clue.text: Fool, as in cards

indicators.note: the word as sits in the cards word

parts.note: jacks are court cards in a pack

explanation.surface: Someone is foolish when it comes to card games.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey and, by extension, a stupid person, which is a fool.

clue.text: Stall, as Spanish car

definitions.meaning: a stall is a ... in the front part of a theatre
A car maker based in Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish car stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre stall is a place to sit, and SEAT is the Spanish motor company.

clue.text: Good old girl in a revolutionary, hardly heard?

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the pieces from old to a are read backwards

parts.note: a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A good old girl caught up with a revolutionary is hardly ever heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a person but signals the turnaround, giving ANISSIMO. PI for good comes from pious, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, pianissimo means very softly, played so quietly it can barely be heard.

clue.text: Sell nonsense in head, there's nothing in it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the head word

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: nonsense suggests letters made senseless, so sell is scrambled

explanation.surface: A salesman pitches nonsense with an empty head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense' scrambles the four letters into ULLSE. The definition is the mathematical idea of a set with no members.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the empty set contains no elements at all, which is what this term names.

clue.text: Lively, seen to keep slowing down

indicators.note: the seen word keeps the musical abbreviation inside it

parts.note: spied means seen
rit is short for ritardando, the musical direction for slowing down

explanation.surface: Something lively has been noticed slowing down.
explanation.walkthrough: RIT, for ritardando, is a musical term many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means full of energy and vigour, so it is a synonym of lively.

clue.text: Vicious in a swarm, moreover

indicators.note: the punk's first name goes in the swarm word

parts.note: a swarm is a mass of bees
Sid Vicious was bass player of the Sex Pistols

explanation.surface: A vicious creature in a swarm adds extra danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' is not an adjective: it is Sid Vicious, the punk musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and moreover both mean in addition, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Having lost semicircular shape, flower is flatter

indicators.note: having lost means the flower word drops a letter

parts.note: a buttercup is a yellow wild flower
the letter C is shaped like a half circle

explanation.surface: A flower that has lost its round cup shape is flatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like an adjective about the squashed flower but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to praise them insincerely, an idiom for flatter.

clue.text: See 20
Bearer of gifts controlling racket is an old revolutionary

indicators.note: Santa controls the next pieces by holding them inside

parts.note: Santa brings presents at Christmas
a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: A gift-bringer runs a racket, and is a former revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandinistas were the Nicaraguan revolutionary movement that took power in 1979.

clue.text: Tailor so in demand if no member in a suit

indicators.note: to tailor is to cut and alter, so these words' letters are recut into a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor is so busy that no clubman in a suit goes without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' and 'suit' suggest clothing; the suit is one of the four in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card from the red suit of a pack, here the nine, is one member of that suit.

clue.text: Girl evidently one of my solutions?

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, as in the actress Bergman
every solution of a crossword is entered in the setter's grid, so read as two words this says where it sits

explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN GRID, the second reading describes any answer in the puzzle, this one included.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a female given name, and an answer sits in the grid of squares.

clue.text: Punched by right hand of Dempsey, strong thing felled — end of fight!

indicators.note: the felled tree is punched by a letter thrust into it
a felled tree is knocked flat, so the tree word is turned round

parts.note: the oak is proverbially strong, as in 'hearts of oak'

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A boxer's mighty opponent is felled by a punch from Jack Dempsey's right.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dempsey was a 1920s world heavyweight boxing champion; Y from his name goes into KAO, the oak reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayo is the spelt-out form of KO, a knockout that ends a boxing bout.

clue.text: Love in man making beastly noises

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
the king is a man in chess

explanation.surface: A man in love behaves like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting sound made by pigs, one example of an animal's noise.

clue.text: Tangle in mobile transmitter finally sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out suggests putting into a different order, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of transmitter

explanation.surface: A tangle in a mobile phone mast is finally fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to involve someone in a conflict, to entangle them in it.

clue.text: Hard thing to get live screening working

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the existing word screens the working word inside it

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A tough job to get a live broadcast up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone is hard, rigid tissue in the skeleton, so it is a fair hard thing.

clue.text: In the end, vote was carried — break down!

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of vote

parts.note: rode means was carried, as on a horse or bus

explanation.surface: The vote was finally carried, so breaking things down.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, a synonym of to break down.

clue.text: In eating droppings, function as dinosaur

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the pieces go inside the first word

parts.note: in is taken as written, its two letters split around the rest
guano is bird or bat droppings
a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: An animal that eats droppings serves as a dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, one of the first identified.
